Prediction_retrieved_article_name_35: Title: Typological Study On the Workplace Faith Fellowship In Its Three Stages of Historical Development in Korea, Abstract: I. INTRODUCTION A. Posing of Problem and the Task of Study The National Statistical Office reported that about 22,219,000 workers are employed nationwide by the September, 2002. This numeric reaches 46.6% of the whole population in Korea. Recent report says that workers feel discouraged and unsecured because of the hostile working environment, limitless competition, structural injustice of industrial society, economic and societal conflict between the rich and the poor, psychological stress and tension, collapse of family and virtue system, and, blurring of the ethical sensitivity in the workplace. It is not surprising therefore to hear from the groups of age in 20' and 30' complaining of their unstable job and future. 'For where two or three are gathered together in my name, I am there in the midst of them' (Mt. 18:20). So many believers have experienced hope and consolation from this text. The text gives not only psychological easiness but also Chris tian vision of vocation that the workplace is the one in which Christ's presence is to be experienced and witnessed. Workplace Faith Fellowship has been the place in which believers are exposed to the concrete real world and encouraged to create and participate in the mystical visible body of Christ, and called to share Christian life in a hostile real world of selfishness, competition, and injustice. It has challenged believers to live with honesty and responsibility the wholistic Christian life supposed to be accomplished through the interconnected structures of family, church, and work place. Considering of its original vision, however, future of the WF appears to be not so hopeful because of the accelerating process of secularization in society. For the writer devoting to the workplace ministry in the Holy Love Church Furniture Company last ten years, current situation is discouraging. How could I revitalize and realize the original vision of the workplace mission? How could I form the faith community in workplace in which believers are challenged to express and create their Christian identity? How could believers be more faithful to Christ's simple words like these: 'Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature' (Mark 16:15); 'You are the salt of the earth but if the salt loses its flavor, how shall it be seasoned? It is then good for nothing but to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by men' (Matthew 5:13). Task of the study is to characterize and evaluate the activities and influence of WFs by using four typologies the writer creates, that is, the worship-centered, the Bible study-centered, the mission-centered, and fellowship-centered, from theological and sociological perspectives, with its three stages of historical development in view. Motif of the study is to help members, leaders, prospective leaders of WF and church leadership confronting ones' history and thereby revitalizing their self-identity in a new way. B. Methodology and the Scope of the Study The study depends on literary analysis of diverse materials from WF and visitation. In Introduction, task and motif of the study will be revealed. Scope of study will be defined. In Chapter II, theoretical ground of WF will be laid, historically, theologically, and sociologically. Historical origins of three categories of WF especially in connection with its leadership style be introduced historically. Theological principles or assumptions of WF will be analyzed in terms of the nature of laity, stewardship, and mission of sending. In sociological analysis, the writer will deal with the value of vocation in diverse perspectives. Chapter III, IV and V deal with history of the WF in its three stages of development: the early (1950'-1970'), the middle (1980'-1990'), and the present (2000-present). Activities in each stage will be explored and characterized in four typologies: the worship centered, the Bible study centered, the mission centered, and the fellowship-diakonia centered, evaluated from theological and sociological perspective, and, summarized critically. II. Theoretical Reflection on Workplace Faith Fellowship A. Historical Reflection The writer analyzes the history of Korean WF in four typologies of the worship centered, the Bible Study Centered, mission centered, and fellowship centered. Four typologies are categorized in terms of the primary concerns and focuses of activities of diverse groups of WF. Though not adopted as a categorizing typology in the thesis, another perspective to categorize WFs would be worth being remarked. It is related to the question of leadership, that is, 'who takes initiative to run WF. 1. Independent Workplace Faith Fellowship Historical origin of WF is known to be a prayer meeting held in Dansung Sa (movie theater) run at that time by Byuksan Co. in 1956. Initiative of this meeting was taken by a devote Christian owner of Byuksan Co.. Theater was open to public on Sunday. And Christians of employees in the company couldn't attend Sunday Worship Service. The owner felt deeply sorry about this situation, finally decided to provide certain space and time (one of weekday) for employees to have opportunity to have service. Though not systematically organized and given space for more creative and extended activities compared to WF today, WF in Dansung Sa is a historical phenomena in Korean christian soil in which worship service celebrated in the church on Sunday is the normative considered biblical and therefore effective. Characteristic of this type of WF is that the owner of the company takes initiative and the activities are restricted more or less within that company. 2. Workplace Mission Association In the pluralistic secular city like Seoul, there are so many big companies, officially not affiliated to any religion. It is hard in this case to get any help for Christian activities from companies, for example. Under this circumstance, there comes up individual Christians, forming an areal christian network which could be called WF. Usually they ask churches in area to provide space and sometimes leadership for meeting. The meeting held at Chonkyo Methodist Church in 1979 is the one in this kind. They first called the meeting as 'Thursday workplace church' because they met at Thursday lunchtime. Members of this meeting introduced their activities around the area, invited other Christian workers to the Easter Service in 1980, and decided to develop 'Thursday workplace church' into 'Workplace Mission Association.' This type of WF has been established since then in big cities, now reaching the nationwide networking of 38 areal organizations by now. In this type of WF, leadership or the initiative is taken by christian workers' network voluntarily established, but with strong relationship with one church in the area who provides meeting space, financial support, and some part of leadership. 3. Workplace Church Worship Workplace Church Worship is a type of meeting in which a certain church takes full initiative in making organization, funding, and providing leadership. The meeting usually origins as a result of mission project of an urban church for the area. Youngrak Presbyterian church began this type of mission project September 5 1969. Church invited workers of Ssang Yong Cement, Bbaek general hospital, Jungbu police station and began worship service at lunch time every Friday. In this type of WP, leadership is under a local church. B. Theological Reflection 1. Theology of Laity Theological ground of WF appears to be theology of laity which is based on the doctrine of priesthood of believers reclaimed by Martin Luther. Luther argued that the only mediator is Jesus Christ and christians baptized have grace of privilege to participate in Christ's priesthood as his visible body in this world. This means that every christian has a duty and privilege to proclaim gospel and offer a prayer of intercession in every place and time, offering spiritual and living worship. Priesthood and apostolic right is not just restricted to the church institution (ordained clergy). Priesthood is to be reinterpreted and applied to all believers in Jesus Christ. The doctrine of priesthood of believers is the ground of the theology of laity and theological justification of WF. What is the biblical meaning of the term 'laity'? As 'laos,' in Greek, it indicates people of God including both clergy and believers not ordained. The term 'laity' is a glorious word because people of God is nothing other than a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people made to proclaim the mighty acts of him who call themselves out of darkness into his marvelous light (1 Peter 2:9). In the early stage of the Christian history, laity means community of believers including apostles, prophets, teachers, deacons, and others given diverse gifts from Holy Spirit, only later, coming to be degraded when it began to indicate a group of believers unordained, passive, derivative and secondary compared to the ordained in the mission of the church. Theology of laity based upon the doctrine of priesthood of believers appears to be implied or assumed in activities of WF. 2. Theology of Stewardship Another theological principle of workplace mission comes from Genesis 1: 28: 'have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the bird....' Message is about stewardship assigned and commanded to human being as image of God. Steward is the faithful and prudent manager (Luke 12:42), servants of Christ and steward of God's mysteries (1 Cor. 4:1), guardians and trustees, blameless (Gal. 4:2). To serve the world as Christ did is one of theological principles which could explain WF's activities in meaningful way. 3. Theology of 'Being Sent' Jesus Christ trained his disciples for three years, sending them to the world. In John 17:18 reading 'As you have sent me into the world, so I have sent them onto the world,' what we see is the special relationship among God, Jesus Christ and disciples, the relationship characterized as 'sending' and 'sent.' God sent Jesus and Jesus sent disciples. Message is about mission and the importance of the relation between the one who send and the one who is sent. Sender gives full authority to the one who is sent. The one to be sent represents the sender in full scale. Jesus also commands to his disciples just before ascension: 'Go therefore and make disciples of all nations' (Mt. 28:19). This command of mission is passed over to members of WF through the disciples. WF is community to be sent to make disciples by God in and through Jesus Christ in this world, that is, in workplace. Being sent is an important theological perspective to have members of WF see their vocation with responsibility and faith. C. Sociological Reflection Korean war (1950-1953) had devastated Korean economy. Poverty was the main issue and problem to be solved to any subsequent political leaderships thereafter. Since 1962 Korean government launched a grand project called '5 Year Economic Development Plan.' The first '5 Year Economic Development Plan' was accomplished during 1962-1966 and the fifth and the last one during 1977-1981. 25 years of national project to elevate economic standard brought rapid and dramatic economic development and prosperity on the one hand, however, moral hazard and loss of ethics of work on the other hand resulting in the IMF period (1997-19998). WF understands their workplace as a mission field and vocation as place in and through which one is called to the service of God and the world. This kind of highly ethical and theological perception of vocation in the consciousness of members of WF came to be known and valued in and out of WF in this one-dimensional wasteland of this kingdom of profit. III. The Initial Stage of Workplace Faith Fellowship (1950s-1980s) A. Worship Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. National Assembly Prayer Breakfast National Assembly Prayer Breakfast was begun in November 1965 by Christian members of the 6th National Assembly, led by Assemblywoman Hyun-Sook Park. The meeting was begun to better love brothers and sisters in Christ, to worship, and was started with the prayer that 'His will be done' in our nation 'as in Heaven.' In May of 1968, the National Assembly Prayer Breakfast and the Korean Prayer Breakfast Committees jointly established National Prayer Breakfast, an annual event where the President, prominent figures of the three departments of the government, and other leaders of different spheres of influence, gathered to pray. Those attending this Prayer Breakfast, despite their unique positions as members of the Assembly, approached the workplace with a firm sense of Christian duty, and the event sublimated into one in which true workplace worship occurred. Their main activity was their Prayer Breakfasts that were held on the first Wednesdays of each month at 7:30 am in the National Assembly Prayer Room (13206), during which the members held service and shared breakfast. They also held service on the days regular as well as extraordinary Assembly meetings were called to order. What is specially noteworthy is that even after the Christian members of the Assembly in opposing parties had confronted each other in fierce debates, they would always worship as one in Christ, giving honor to God and sharing love in fellowship with one another. 2. National Assembly Prayer Meetings National Assembly Prayer Meetings are a separate WF from National Assembly Breakfast Prayer. This WF had its start when three sisters in Christ (Kyung-Hae Kim, Young-Sook Choi, Chi-Myung Park) met to hold a prayer meeting on October 22, 1976. At the time, with no rooms available in which to have worship, the group of three met in storage rooms, ventilation room, or utility rooms to raise up earnest, tearful prayers. By God's provision they were able to hold their first meeting in their newly obtained permanent prayer room, in basement room 206, on September 12, 1979. The sound of prayer never ceased coming from this room for an entire year. On December 26 1979, the National Assembly Prayer Association's Inaugural General Synod (President: Chang-Lyul Kim) met, and on January 5th 1980 they held an Inaugural Worship Service Sermon: Bishop Gi-Chun Jang). B. Bible Study Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship As Bible study centered WF, Faith Movement for Bankers of the Bank of Korea can be pick up. It had its humble beginnings on August 27, 1975 with three people at the preparatory prayer meeting. On November 26 the same year, they had the Inaugural General Synod and began its growth as a WF. The regulation established at this time, 'We are to spread Biblically grounded Gospel, and in fostering interrelationship among members, give glory to God,' was the purpose of this ministry and now, 20 years after, the same holds. From March 20, 1978 four teams of 40 members committed to group Bible studies began. For those who may wonder, 'Why Bible studies at this particular time?', it could be said that the studies were prompted by the 'New Living' seminar that was started at Bank of We. At the time in 1978, over the course of four days of February 14th to the 17th at the 2nd meeting, an average of 350 people attended every day, making the Bank of Korea auditorium a place where many were touched. As an outflow of such memorable experience Bible study groups sprang up in different departments. As teaching material they used what Pastor Dong-Won Lee (Then Faith Movement for Bankers leader and Pastor of Global Missions Church) provided, 'The 9 Steps of the Creed.' The Bible studies span on average 30 to 40 minutes, and are divided into times of Bible study, prayer, fellowship, and praise. About 80% of the time is spent on the study of the Bible, which is also divided into Bible reading, teaching, and sharing, of which teaching is alloted 50% of the time. Outside the regular meetings, the Bible study members meet to visit and serve at centers for the disabled and senior citizens. They also collect money to celebrate special occasions such as birthdays and promotions, to give farewell gifts to those being transferred, and in addition, many groups jointly go on one day prayer retreats. C. Mission Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship The Missions Society of Seoul Bank is WF that was founded in the midst of much discord and hurt resulting from the merger between Seoul Bank and Sintak Bank in 1976. The group had its beginning as a seemingly inconsiderable prayer meeting. It was Jong-Bok Kim, then central staff member of CCC (Korea Campus Crusade for Christ)6), who had vision of having a group 'Centered ministering lay people at the workplace,' and to help foster the 'growth as a global bank' in order to 'share in the vision of world missions' which made the birth of this group, on January 1977, possible. In September of 1997, this small society grew to include 500 registered members with chapters in Busan, Jam-sil Jun-San Center, L.A., and developed to have different departments specializing in worship Service, evangelism, volunteering, pamphlet missions, and musical praise. To vitalize the regional chapters, advising pastors and/or officers are appointed to go and to take part in their worship services, partake in fellowship, and exchange information, particularly in order to discuss evangelism methods. Those from the main headquarters regularly attend meetings at the chapters and are jointly pushing for business missions. D. Fellowship-Diakonia Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Investment Firms Workplace Faith Fellowship At the starting point of the history of Korean WF, we find the Investment firm WF. On December 27; 1977, Christian employees working in investment firms with a united desire to spread the Gospel in their field established three independent WFs in the old National Theatre in Myoung Dong. The mission statement of the group was to foster the holy fellowship of believers in the realm of investment and to accomplish Jesus Christ's great missions commission. As they remained true to these founding principles and put them to action, the group now consists of 30 investment firms WFs with 3000 members spread over the country, including their four regional chapters in Busan, Gwang Joo, Ool San, and Dae Gu, and becomes an influential missions organization. 2. Youngrak Church's Workplace Church Worship Different from unit WFs with leadership taken by a particular WF and meeting held during the weekday, for workplace church worship type of WF, leadership is provided by the local church. This local church provides with leadership, fund, meeting place and other ones in need. This is immediately related to city church's mission strategy to reaching out surrounding regional community. This WP started by Youngnak Church (Senior Pastor: Chul-Shin Lee) located in Ju-Dong, Seoul, and also that first of its kind in Korea, celebrates its 35th anniversary in 2004. During lunch break of yet another ordinary Friday September 5th 1969, this kind of WF was offered to the workers in the area who were employed at places such as Ssang Young Cement, Bbaek General Hospital, and the Junbu Police Station. 10 people had attended the first worship service but at the present some 200 people have become regulars. E. Evaluation 1. Sociological and Theological Evaluation The economic state of Korea in its beginnings as a modern country was dismal. After the tragedy of the fratricidal Korean War, country faces a great hardship. Factories, buildings, railroads, and other facilities of value were all destroyed, and the toll on human life was tremendous. According to data from an organization, civilian casualties soared as high as 244, 663 for South Korea alone, higher for North Korea with 406,000 dead, with 303,212 missing, and 680,000 wounded or injured. No doubt, it was a period of great darkness. Notwithstanding, WF that was started in 1956 sublimated the deep hurts from the war with faith, and took on the great task of spreading the Gospel, and of serving society. When giving a theological (ecclesiological) evaluation of the WF in its early years, one should make it from the theological perspective of 'sending.' God is the subject of missions. God's mission began with the sending of His son Jesus Christ into this world, and the love that sent His only son was not limited to Israel or a certain nation but was meant for all of humanity. The theological perspective of 'sending' characterizes the nature of activities of WF in its initial stage of historical development. Also thanks to this theology the worship, service format centered on the leadership of minister gave way to that grounded upon the leadership of laity. This theology justifies the fact that worship could be brought out from the church building into the outside world. 2. Overall Evaluation It is worth noting that WF in its early stage was established out of the poor lay leaderships, inferior working environment in which general ethos is so opposite from that of Christian vision of living, and absence of more or less articulated theological ground. Namely, it would be likely that the most active minority are not in the mainstream in the workplace. This would probably result in WF's somewhat restricted influence on workplace or the society. Attempting to classify the various WFs from the early years, the writer suffers most because of rarity of materials answering questions like these: 'How many leaders were working?' 'how were they equipped with more technical knowledge,' 'how were new comers trained and nurtured?' 'how many people worked actively?' IV. The Middle Stage of the Workplace Faith Fellowship (1981-1990) A. Worship Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Sung-Ae Church Furniture Company Sung-Ae Church Furniture Company was founded on 1967. Company motto was 'Safely and Faithfully,' 'Diligently and Wisely,' 'Enduring Faith.' The company places priority on WF worship. In 1977, after the Sung-Ae Furniture Company Factory was rebuilt for expansion, Thanksgiving Service (sermon: Pastor Jung-Soo Park) was held. From this worship, the company's WF worship was decided to take on a new form as 'Monday Service,' with the purpose of offering the first hour of the workweek to God. Of course, there have been services at Sung-Ae from its founding, but it was in a form that merely followed class meeting order of Methodist Church. Main Activities focused on missions in and abroad, miscellaneous activities, which would actualize philosophy of management: 'Glory to God. 2. Ebenezer of Samsung Electronics Ebenezer is the name of WF in Samsung Electronics, an affiliated enterprise of Samsung Group, located in Gi-Heung of Kyoung-Gi Provence. It started when Chul Jin Lee (at present Professor of Nano Technology at Han Yang University), Kwang-Hee Yang, and a few other brothers met to hold worship services together in 1984. Main activities of this WF is as follow: regular meetings (Tuesdays every week at the women's dormitory Baek-Hap dong education center in basement, 6pm); prayer meetings at Paul Prayer Center; missions abroad Ebenezer retreat. 3. Christian Workplace Faith Fellowship of Seoul Subway Corporation The Christian WF of Seoul Subway Corporation held its initiation meeting on June 29, 1984, and held the Christian WF worship commemorating its founding September 15, 1984. They named the community as 'Christian WF of Seoul Subway Corporation,' and elected Han Mo Jung as president, and, celebrated its inaugural worship servide with Rev. Yong Gi Cho (Yoido Full Gospel Church) as speaker on October 6th 1984. Jae Myung Kim (CEO) and other 500 people were present. They opened a sanctuary in Sin Chun Station (subway line 2) on October 20, and began its WF activities. Main Activities are as follow: regular monthly services; inaugural worship wervice; Christmas Tree Lighting worship service; relief services; funding missionaries abroad and/or Church Planting efforts; funding concert choir; coalition report publication; spreading Gospel at workplace; funding workplace mission general assemblies; managing and running sanctuary and offices. B. Bible Study Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Business Bible Belt ('BBB') BBB had its beginning when around 40 workers in Myong Dong business area gathered together to study the Bible on January of 1990, to be trained and nurtured in faith, and to accomplish discipleship fully and effectively in workplace given to them. This has become an extensive organization. This WF has 1,300 participating members in cities of Seoul (areas of Myoung Dong, Gwang Hwa Moon, Seoul Station, Gang Nam, Yoido) and is active in other cities like Chun An, Dae Gu, Dae Jun, Ik San. It is interesting to note that this WF has its chapter even in Singapore. BBB's strategy for mission is as follow: living out a life of evangelism in the workplace; establishing a small size of groups of Bible study; cultivating leadership; working together for spreading the Gospel. C. Mission Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Workplace Faith Fellowship Federation of Incheon: WF Federation of Incheon was established May 5, 1988, with following objectives: sanctification of Incheon through strengthening relations among various WF groups, and through vitalizing workplace ministries fostering a Christian culture in the Incheon workplace and its society through individual WF's attempt to elevate quality of educational service activities, vitalize the Christian spirituality helping members living out of faith having unification of WFs movements as the group's main concerns putting to action the slogan such as 'Offer Incheon to God! Sanctification of Incheon through workplace mission! Glory to God by faith and missions!';spreading the Gospel in the workplace by the joining of 100 individual WFs; funding and commissioning missionaries abroad. 2. Workplace Faith Fellowship Federation of the City of Yuh Soo: WT Federation of the city of Yuh Soo, at first emerging as an ecumenical laity movement, was established in its present form on January 12, 1984 with Soon Ahn Kim as its first president. Now it numbers 1500 in 28 WFs. Its slogan is 'Workplace Missions! Evangelize the Region! Glory to God!' with practical objectives such as: evangelization of the region through vitalization of workplace mission; creation of Christian spirituality in workplace by living out the Christian spirituality; unity of Church by the strengthening of interrelations within WFs. 3. Workplace Faith Fellowship Federation of Kyoung Buk and the city of Dae Gu. On March 3, 1990, a planning committee of 11 members for the founding of WF federation of Kyung Buk and the city of Dae Gu was formed with having Inaugural General Assembly started at Don Il Church on May 19, 1990. This WF federation includes Korean Electric WF as well as thirteen other WFs. Main activities are as follow: opening of Misba Public Square Special Testimony; providing Bible studies for workers; publishing and distributing evangelistic reading material for the purpose of spreading the Gospel in the workplace; making evangelistic publications to indict idolatry culture in Dae-Gu Kyung-Buk. 4. Fellowship-Diakonia Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. The United Korea Energies Workplace Faith Fellowship 'Heralds of Light, triumph over the darkness' (Korean hymnal. 259). On the day of the National Federation Meeting Han-Nam University in the city of Dae Jun, there was an urgent motion to initiate missionary work by giving up lunch for a month for the Lord. Immediately members of WFs from all over the nation were invited to join in the vision and to facilitate an efficient management of ministries. For the task, WFs of different regions, a National Federation of WF and WF association were established and officers elected. Korea Drivers Mission Association On December 16, 1981 the Korea Drivers Mission Society was founded, and on April 16, 1985 their office moved to the Road Traffic Safety Association. Main activities are as follow: preaching the Gospel to drivers (Evangelism through each company, restaurants for drivers, and Model Drivers Association); evangelism of passengers via distribution of evangelic publications; broadcasting ministries (recommending listening to the Christian Broadcasting Station, and Far-East Broadcasting Station); having praise and sermon tapes ready in the vehicle to allow passengers to listen; hold Evangelical Praise Competitions. E. Evaluation 1 Sociological and Theological Evaluation It would not be a stretch to say that phenomenal flourishing of Korea WFs in this middle period was a beneficiary of the impressive economic growth of the 1980s and 90s. After the Korean War, government adopted forceful economic policies, and accomplished amazing task which could be called 'the miracle of Han River.' Korea has been changed drastically from the agricultural nation to the highly developed industrial nation in this period. 2. General Evaluation WFs in this period were under the situation of astounding economic growth and development. It is to be noted, however, that economic growth brought about divisions and conflicts among the various groups of the economic classes. WF concerns this social conflicts in workplace. WFs were growing in number at this period. Yet along with this accomplishment we find that there are slight problems as well; surprisingly, there are no, and if any very few, cases of successful evangelization of non-believing co-workers in the company. It seems that the priorities had been shifted. It reminds me, as it is depicted in Acts 6:1-2, of how even those of the early church, after there was a great revival and masses became believers, found themselves in a situation where they were struggling with disunity in regards to relief work, as opposed to clinging harder to the most important things, that is, prayer and the Word: Now during those days, when the disciples were increasing in number, the Hellenists complained against the Hebrews because their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution of food. And the twelve called together the whole community of the disciples and said, 'It is not right that we should neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables.(Acts 6:1-2) Similarly we can see in this period that WFs put more emphasis on the derivative elements rather than on the most important, which was the saving of souls in the workplace. In addition, I would like to point out that much of missions of WF in the workplace was accomplished under the lay leadership, meaning that there decreased a feeling of necessity of the existence of the ordained ministry for the workplace and of the connection between WFs and local churches. I would call this period as 'the Miracle of WF.' V. The Present Stage of the Workplace Faith Fellowship (1991-present) A. Worship Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship On October 12, 2003, the staff workers of True Love Haven Fire Kiln Sauna, Sung Joon Jung and his family, and employees at the Jung Gun Public Company gathered for their first worship service together. They held their Inaugural Worship service on May 23, 2004, with Methodist District Superintendent Haang Sub Jin giving a sermon entitled 'A Desired Church.' The first regular worship service, its format taking after a conventional Sunday service, took place on October 12 with 20 people in attendance. Though similar in form of worship, workplace mission is the focus and priority in this group. Their objective is to help workers lead an upright spiritual life and to encourage workers approach their profession and tasks at the workplace with a 'Christian honesty.' B. Bible Study Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship New Life Training Center ('NLTC') is at the core of a movement representing this type of WF in the period. Purpose of NLTC is Carrying out training programs for mission and raising up disciples in all socio-economic classes; providing helpful resources and strategies to carry out any related ministries; mobilizing believers through a standardized, simple, and easily transmitted methodologies Contents of NLTC Training is as follow: maturing of individual spiritual life; skills for basic ministerial work; expansion of vision; relationship with local church; fulfillment of great commission. The training is composed of four steps of preaching Gospel, nurturing, training, and sending forth. Educational objecitves are as follow: discernable individual spiritual growth; maturing of character with that of spiritual disciplines (QT, Bible studies, prayer); developing of various ministerial skills; deepening ownership of the vision for the spreading of Gospel in each region, in each class, and ultimately all over the world; developing of leadership. C. Mission Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Korean Christian Bureaucrat Missions Association The Korean Christian Bureaucrat Missions Association was established on November 14, 1998 (General Government Building 19th floor) with 625 members in attendance. The purpose for the founding of this organization lies in their desire to spread the Gospel and Christian spirituality in the realm of public office. Main activities are as follow: formation of mission society in the level of city and providence (March-Oct of 1999); formulating workplace missions strategy and providing a seminar for that (11/27/1999); Christian government employees's mountain prayer meeting for national unity (10/15/1999) Especially concern was laid on structuring of mission strategies, discipleship training system and application strategy with vision to train workplace missionaries. 2. Workplace Faith Fellowship of The Department of Financial Administration and Economy WF of the Department of Financial Administration and Economy had its beginning in December 23, 1994 with the appointment of pastor Gwan Young Kim as Senior Pastor, and Hong Gi Kim as its president in March 3, 1998. The leadership of the group is divided into the president and manager, treasurer, and praise team. Their regular Thursday Bible Study meetings (12-1pm) are held in Language Room 1 of Ahn Nae Dong basement, and their Wednesday Worship Services (12-1pm) and Friday Prayer Meetings (8-gam) in 1-Dong Room 105 in the basement. (Matthews 25:36), 2,000 correction officers take pride in the fact that they are missionaries at the edge, quietly carry on their task to serve wherever they are, and are putting in all their devotion to show that God's kingdom expands even into the prison cells. E. Evaluation 1. Sociological and Theological Evaluation Korea in the 1990s used the authoritarian model of development and experienced an unrivaled growth rate which placed it on 11th place in the world as a powerful international trading country, and in 1995 the country entered into the age of 1 million dollar GNP (at the time it was 9,000,000 won), allowing them to become an OECD member in 1996, which all in turn, made this member of the Four Asian Dragons a subject of research as a model of 3rd world development. Jordan's manufacturing industry must establish adequate methods to address sustainability concerns and increase big-data analytics usage. Title: MDAIC - a Six Sigma implementation strategy in big data environments, Abstract:

Purpose

Modern production facilities produce large amounts of data. The computational framework often referred to as big data analytics has greatly improved the capabilities of analyses of large data sets. Many manufacturing companies can now seize this opportunity to leverage their data to gain competitive advantages for continuous improvement. Six Sigma has been among the most popular approaches for continuous improvement. The data-driven nature of Six Sigma applied in a big data environment can provide competitive advantages. In the traditional Six Sigma implementation - define, measure, analyze, improve and control (DMAIC) problem-solving strategy where a human team defines a project ahead of data collection. This paper aims to propose a new Six Sigma approach that uses massive data generated to identify opportunities for continuous improvement projects in a manufacturing environment in addition to human input in a measure, define, analyze, improve and control (MDAIC) format.

Design/methodology/approach

The proposed Six Sigma strategy called MDAIC starts with data collection and process monitoring in a manufacturing environment using system-wide monitoring that standardizes continuous, attribute and profile data into comparable metrics in terms of “traffic lights.” The classifications into green, yellow and red lights are based on pre-control charts depending on how far a measurement is from its target. The proposed method monitors both process parameters and product quality data throughout a hierarchical production system over time. An attribute control chart is used to monitor system performances. As the proposed method is capable of identifying changed variables with both spatial and temporal spaces, Six Sigma teams can easily pinpoint the areas in need to initiate Six Sigma projects.

Findings

Based on a simulation study, the proposed method is capable of identifying variables that exhibit the biggest deviations from the target in the Measure step of a Six Sigma project. This provides suggestions of the candidates for the improvement section of the proposed MDAIC methodology.

Originality/value

This paper proposes a new approach for the identifications of projects for continuous improvement in a manufacturing environment. The proposed framework aims to monitor the entire production system that integrates all types of production variables and the product quality characteristics.

Title: Early Detection of Hypoglycemia in Type 1 Diabetes Using Heart Rate Variability Measured by a Wearable Device, Abstract:

OBJECTIVE

Changes in heart rate variability (HRV) occur at the initiation of hypoglycemia due to sympathetic nervous system activity. We investigated the use of HRV detection by a wearable device as an early alert for hypoglycemia.

This proof-of-principle study included 23 patients with type 1 diabetes (14 women, mean age 42 ± 11 years). Patients wore a VitalConnect HealthPatch for 5 days. Hypoglycemia was defined as glucose ≤70 mg/dL (≤3.9 mmol/L) by fingerstick measurement. HRV was analyzed in standardized periods before the hypoglycemic event.

RESULTS

Sixty-six hypoglycemic events were recorded. Hypoglycemia caused a typical HRV pattern in 36 (55%) of the hypoglycemic events. Eighteen events (27%) showed an atypical pattern. Ten events were unclassified (15%), and two did not display a change in HRV (3%).

CONCLUSIONS

Hypoglycemia causes early changes in HRV that can be detected by a wearable device. Measuring real-time HRV seems promising for early hypoglycemia detection.

Objectives: This study aims to identify a reliable prediction model for Mexico's wholesale electricity market to prevent supply-demand imbalances by analyzing three machine learning models with conformal prediction techniques.  Theoretical Framework: Electricity demand forecasting traditionally uses SARIMAX models or artificial neural networks (ANN)/deep learning (DL). However, SARIMAX models are sensitive to data perturbations, while ANN/DL models face interpretability and computational challenges. Decision tree-based models (LGBM and CatBoost) have emerged as alternatives, offering potential advantages for time series prediction.  Method: The study analyzed electricity demand data from CENACE (2018-2022), using four years for training and one for validation. Title: Deep-Learning-based Cryptanalysis through Topic Modeling, Abstract:

Neural cryptography is a technique that uses neural networks for secure data encryption. Cryptoanalysis, on the other hand, deals with analyzing and decrypting ciphers, codes, and encrypted text without using a real key. Chosen-plaintext cryptanalysis is a subfield of cryptanalysis where both plain text and ciphertext are available and the goal is either to find the encryption technique, the encryption key, or both. This study addresses chosen plaintext cryptanalysis within public key cryptography, to categorize topics of encrypted text. Using a fixed encryption technique and key, the focus was placed on creating a framework that identifies the topic associated with ciphertext, using diverse plaintexts and their corresponding cipher texts. To our knowledge, this is the first time that chosen-plaintext cryptanalysis has been discussed in the context of topic modeling. The paper used deep learning techniques such as CNNs, GRUs, and LSTMs to process sequential data. The proposed framework achieved up to 67% precision, 99% recall, 80% F1-score, and 71% AUPR on a dataset, showcasing promising results and opening avenues for further research in this cryptanalysis subarea.

Title: Adaptive Framework for Deep Learning Based Dynamic and Temporal Topic Modeling from Big Data, Abstract:

Background:

The large amount of data emanated from social media platforms need scalable topic modeling in order to get current trends and themes of events discussed on such platforms. Topic modeling play crucial role in many natural language processing applications like sentiment analysis, recommendation systems, event tracking, summarization, etc.

Objective:

The aim of the proposed work is to adaptively extract the dynamically evolving topics over streaming data, and infer the current trends and get the notion of trend of topics over time. Because of various world level events, many uncorrelated streaming channels tend to start discussion on similar topics. We aim to find the effect of uncorrelated streaming channels on topic modeling when they tend to start discussion on similar topics.

Methods:

An adaptive framework for dynamic and temporal topic modeling using deep learning has been put forth in this paper. The framework approximates online latent semantic indexing constrained by regularization on streaming data using adaptive learning method. The framework is designed using deep layers of feedforward neural network.

Results:

This framework supports dynamic and temporal topic modeling. The proposed approach is scalable to large collection of data. We have performed exploratory data analysis and correspondence analysis on real world Twitter dataset. Results state that our approach works well to extract topic topics associated with a given hashtag. Given the query, the approach is able to extract both implicit and explicit topics associated with the terms mentioned in the query.

Conclusion:

The proposed approach is a suitable solution for performing topic modeling over Big Data. We are approximating the Latent Semantic Indexing model with regularization using deep learning with differentiable ℓ1 regularization, which makes the model work on streaming data adaptively at real-time. The model also supports the extraction of aspects from sentences based on interrelation of topics and thus, supports aspect modeling in aspect-based sentiment analysis.

Topic modeling for short texts is a challenging and interesting problem in the machine learning and knowledge discovery domains. Nowadays, millions of documents published on the internet from various sources. Internet websites are full of various topics and information, but there is a lot of similarity between topics, contents, and total quality of sources, which causes data repetition and gives the user the same information. Another issue is data sparsity and ambiguity because the length of the short text is limited, which causes unsatisfactory results and give irrelevant results to end-users. All these mentioned issues in short texts made an interesting topic for researchers to use machine learning and knowledge discovery techniques to discover underlying topics from a massive amount of data. In this paper, we propose a combination of deep reinforcement learning (RL) and semantics-assisted non-negative matrix factorization model to extract meaningful and underlying topics from short document contents. The main objective of this work is to reduce the problem of repetitive information and data sparsity in short texts to help the users to get meaningful and relevant contents. Furthermore, our propose model reviews an issue of the Seq2Seq approach based on the reinforcement learning perspective and provides a combination of reinforcement learning and SeaNMF formulation using the block coordinate descent algorithm. Moreover, we compare different real-world datasets by using numerical calculation and present a couple of state-of-art models to get better performance on short text document topic modeling. Based on experimental results and comparative analysis, our propose model outperforms the state of art techniques in terms of short document topic modeling.

Title: Evaluation of Real-Time Endogenous Brain-Computer Interface Developed Using Ear-Electroencephalography, Abstract:

While previous studies have demonstrated the feasibility of using ear-electroencephalography (ear-EEG) for the development of brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), most of them have been performed using exogenous paradigms in offline environments. To verify the reliable feasibility of constructing ear-EEG-based BCIs, the feasibility of using ear-EEG should be further demonstrated using another BCI paradigm, namely the endogenous paradigm, in real-time online environments. Exogenous and endogenous BCIs are to use the EEG evoked by external stimuli and induced by self-modulation, respectively. In this study, we investigated whether an endogenous ear-EEG-based BCI with reasonable performance can be implemented in online environments that mimic real-world scenarios. To this end, we used three different mental tasks, i.e., mental arithmetic, word association, and mental singing, and performed BCI experiments with fourteen subjects on three different days to investigate not only the reliability of a real-time endogenous ear-EEG-based BCI, but also its test-retest reliability. The mean online classification accuracy was almost 70%, which was equivalent to a marginal accuracy for a practical two-class BCI (70%), demonstrating the feasibility of using ear-EEG for the development of real-time endogenous BCIs, but further studies should follow to improve its performance enough to be used for practical ear-EEG-based BCI applications.

발전하기 위해서는 전략적인 접근이 필요하다. 우리나라 대학은 사립대학 중심으로 이루어져 있으며, 사립대학의 재정 수입구조는 외부 의존도가 높다. 이로 인해 많은 대학이 생존을 위해 교육수요자의 선호와 정부 정책 변화에 민감하게 반응할 수밖에 없는 실정이다. 그러나 동일한 환경적‧제도적 압력이 모든 대학에 가해지더라도 이에 대응하는 전략은 각 대학의 고유한 특성과 여건에 따라 달라진다. 본 연구에서도 대학 특성에 따라 첨단‧신기술 분야 신규학과와 기존 학과‧전공에서 대상과 분야를 특성화한 신규학과의 생성 양상이 다르게 나타났다. 그리고 첨단‧신기술 분야 및 특성화 신규학과 개설 상위권 대학의 경우, 취업률 측면에서 일정 부분 긍정적인 변화가 관찰되었다. 이는 개별 대학이 자신의 특성을 면밀히 파악하고, 이를 바탕으로 조직 효과성과 생존 가능성을 제고할 수 있는 맞춤형 전략을 수립하여 적극적으로 추진해야 함을 시사한다. 둘째, 매년 신규학과가 누적되어 학과구조를 형성하므로 학과‧전공 변화의 질적 관리가 필요하다. 2007~2022년 동안 연평균 445.06개의 신규학과가 발생하였고, 사립대학, 비수도권 대학, 소규모 대학일수록 전체 학과 수 대비 신규학과 수 비율의 평균이 높아 학과구조 개편이 더욱 빈번하게 이루어졌음을 알 수 있다. 이는 불리한 여건의 대학일수록 외부의 요구나 피드백에 의해 근시안적인 학과‧전공 재편이 발생할 가능성이 높음을 의미한다. 그러나 현재 한국교육개발원과 한국대학교육협의회가 관리하는 학과‧전공 데이터 체계에는 한계가 있어 개별 대학의 학과구조 개편의 질적 수준을 파악하기 어려운 실정이다. 따라서 대학별 학과‧전공 변경 이력과 세부 내용을 직관적으로 파악할 수 있도록 기존 시스템을 보완하거나 재구축할 필요가 있다. 아울러 학과‧전공의 변경 흐름을 체계적으로 모니터링하여 지속적인 질 관리가 이루어지도록 해야 한다. 셋째, 융‧복합 신규학과가 증가하는 추세이므로 융․복합 학과․전공 현황 파악을 위한 분류 방식의 개선이 필요하다. 융‧복합 신규학과는 2015년 이후 생성된 비중이 70.16%에 달할 정도로 시간이 지날수록 증가세가 뚜렷해졌다. 그러나 한국교육개발원, 통계청, 한국대학교육협의회의 현행 학과분류체계는 융‧복합 학과‧전공의 특성을 정확히 반영하는 데 한계가 있다. 융‧복합 학과‧전공의 실태를 정확히 파악하기 위해서는 융‧복합 여부뿐만 아니라 어떤 분야 간 융‧복합이 이루어졌는지 알 수 있어야 한다. 이를 위해 한국교육개발원의 학과분류체계가 현재의 트리 구조를 유지한다면, 학과코드는 기존과 같이 주된 분야를 기준으로 부여하되, 융‧복합된 나머지 분야에 대해서는 제2~3분류를 추가 지정하는 방안을 고려해 볼 수 있다. 넷째, 첨단‧신기술 분야 인재 양성이 강조되면서 관련 신규학과가 급증하고 있으므로 국가 차원의 인력양성 규모 파악이 필요하다. 2015년 이후 생성된 첨단‧신기술 분야 신규학과의 비중이 82.63%에 달하였는데, 이는 정부의 정책과 외부 환경변화에 대응한 대학의 생존전략이 맞물린 결과로 해석된다. 그러나 첨단‧신기술의 범위와 목록은 정책목표와 사회‧기술환경 변화에 따라 달라져 왔으며, 인력양성 정책 수립의 기초가 되는 인력 수요 및 공급 규모에 대한 정확한 추정이 이루어지지 못하고 있다. 따라서 첨단‧신기술 분야 학과‧전공에 대한 합리적인 기준을 정립하여 첨단‧신기술 분야별 인력양성 규모를 정확하게 파악할 필요가 있다. 또한 2023년부터 시행된 개인정보 기반 고등교육통계조사를 바탕으로, 학생별 수강 이력을 활용하여 종합적인 인력 규모를 산정하는 방안을 모색할 필요가 있다. 다섯째, 대학이 사회에서 필요로 하는 인재를 효과적으로 양성할 수 있도록 대학 혁신을 위한 정부의 지원이 강화되어야 한다. 대학은 변화에 적응하고 사회수요에 부응하기 위해 신규학과를 개설해 왔지만, 이를 위해서는 재원이 필요하다. 하지만 현재 대학들이 직면한 재정난으로 인해 혁신 추진에 어려움을 겪고 있다. 이에 우수대학에는 경쟁력 제고를 위해 중점 지원하는 한편, 변화 의지와 잠재력은 있으나 재정이 열악한 대학에는 초기 지원을 통해 내부 혁신 동력을 유발할 필요가 있다. 이러한 차별화된 재정지원 정책은 대학 간 격차를 완화하고 고등교육 전반의 질적 수준을 높이는 데 기여할 것이다. 나아가 대학 생태계 전체에 선순환 구조가 정착된다면, 학생 개인의 역량 증진은 물론 국가 경쟁력 강화에도 이바지할 수 있을 것으로 기대된다., Source: Prediction_retrieved_article_name_31: Title: 컨벤션 개최지 선호도 측정지표 개발을 통한 포지셔닝 비교 연구 : MDS 분석을 중심으로, Abstract: The objective of this study is twofold. The first objective is to derive the preference indicator of convention destinations by using the Delphi technique and the second is to provide an empirical analysis(실증분석) on the positioning of Asia’s leading convention destinations. The findings and results of this study will contribute to intensifying Korea’s competitiveness as a convention destination by providing for a competitive policy and strategy regarding destination marketing for convention.&#xD; The four specific research objectives of the study are as follows. &#xD; First, it aims to establish the theoretical foundation for developing the preference indicator of convention destinations and comparative research on positioning through analysis of previous research related to selection attribute, competitiveness, preference, and positioning. Second, it aims to develop the preference indicator of convention destinations by the Delphi technique and to verify the validity of it. Third, through the developed preference indicator, it aims to provide a comparative analysis of the positioning of Asia's leading countries as convention destinations. Finally, it offers policy insights for a competitive positioning strategy for Korea as a convention destination, based on the results of comparative analysis on positioning of the destinations.&#xD; The theoretical basis was established through the literature review on the subject, while the preference indicator was developed through the Delphi technique and quantitative method. The developed indicator and MDS analysis method were used to compare and analyze the positioning strategies of seven convention destinations in Asia. &#xD; The followings are the major implications of the study.&#xD; The literature review and open-ended preliminary research and the survey of CMPs(certified meeting professionals) and meeting and convention specialists elicited 67 convention destination-preferred factors, which were later narrowed down to the final 33 factors after conducting the three Delphi studies. Consequently, the preference indicator of 17 criteria and 6 factors was developed after going through verification of the indicators’ validity. Also, cross- validation was retained to ensure that it can be used as a standardized indicator to measure the preference of convention destinations. &#xD; Accommodation/food &amp; beverage service, communication service, event management expertise featured variance explanation, among the measurement factors (event management expertise, price, convention destination attractiveness, communication service, accommodation/beverage service, conference center facility). Each factor comprises three management expertise criteria(event management expertise, local organizing committee's management ability, up-to-date audio-visual equipment), three cost criteria(charge for convention center, hotel and transportation), three convention destination attractiveness (Extra-conference opportunities) criteria (tour before and after conference, convention destinations promotion, reputation, approachable/abundant shopping area), three internationalization criteria(simultaneous translation equipment, staff's language skills, CVB service), three accommodation/food &amp; beverage service criteria(accommodation capacity, the quality of hotel service, food &amp; beverage service related to convention), two site environment criteria(size of the main conference room, a small scale conference room). Relatively important questions are accommodation capacity, convention planner's wide experience, and the quality of hotel service, organization and management ability of local organizing committee, language skills of local staff, hotel room rates, convention destination promotion, reputation (image) and food &amp; beverage service related to convention.&#xD; Second, KYST, PROFIT, PREFMAP, MDPREP, CORRESPONDENCE Analysis were made in order to compare the convention destinations’ positioning of Asia's leading countries. The result showed that a similar image is formed among Korea, Japan, Thailand, and Malaysia, while Singapore, China, and India have an independent image as a convention destination. Korea and Japan achieved superiority in the convention center environment while Singapore has its comparative advantage in communication service. However, Singapore and Japan featured high competitiveness in accommodation, food &amp; beverage service, convention destination attractiveness and management expertise. Korea held a dominant position over Thailand, Malaysia, India, and China, despite its inferiority to Singapore and Japan. The cost is the key factor to Thailand and Malaysia's major competitiveness, while no particular competitive advantage has been identified for India and China. &#xD; As the analysis of preference ideal point indicates that Singapore is the most preferred nation, followed by Japan. On the other hand, the least preferred destinations are India and China. Korea is less preferred to Singapore and Japan but holds a similar position with Thailand and Malaysia. &#xD; Singapore is ranked as the first preferred convention destination in every type of conference and followed by Japan, Korea and Thailand. India, Malaysia, and China turned out to be least preferred regardless of the type of conference. It shows that preference of convention destinations is deeply related to the overall preference of a nation, not to a particular type of conference. &#xD; Finally, correspondence analysis on the type of conference and preferred destination was made. Whereas Singapore was the most preferred destination with the exception of academic conference, Japan acquired relatively high preference in business conference and incentive travel. Korea and Thailand were favored in terms of business conference. However, Malaysia and India lacked preference in overall areas, not selected as preferred nations in accordance with any type of conference. An exception was China, a preferred nation for exhibition, which showed difference in individual inclination of working level staff.&#xD; The findings of the study have the following implications. First of all, the existing selection attributes play an important role in evaluating preference of the convention destination. Second, working level staff’s perception about the preference indicator differs from individual to individual. Third, some of the traditionally preferred selection attributes are losing its importance, as meeting planners and specialists are giving more weight on convention management expertise.&#xD; Regarding the analysis of convention destination positioning, the study also determines several strategic tasks for securing Korea’s competitiveness as convention destination. First, Korea is required to create a pan-governmental master plan to compete with Singapore in order to be the most competitive convention destination in Asia. Second, Korea must develop a competitive advantage factor and positioning strategy to differentiate it further from Thailand, which is a rival competitor in overall and business conference preference. &#xD; Third, Korea needs to come up with a competitive strategy that differentiates it from Japan to overcome similarities in national image and advantage factors between the two countries. &#xD; In order to strengthen Korea's convention destination competitiveness, the results and finding of the study were reviewed and discussed. As a result, practical policy suggestions were presented. &#xD; First, building a strong convention brand is required. Second, the convention website run by Korea Tourism Organization should be optimized for meeting customers' needs through selection and concentration. Third, systematic statistics management is required for the policy framework through estimating the scale of the convention industry and generating reliable convention statistics, which all highlights the need for establishing the total convention service center. Fourth, both internal and external capacities need to be reinforced for attracting new conventions. Fifth, currently existing convention-attracting and hosting support service are required to flourish a ripple effect to the local economy by attracting conferences related to newly-emerging fields (scientific technology, agriculture and forestry, animal husbandry, maritime and fishery, public health, space industry). Sixth, a high value convergence convention connected with medical care, Hallyu (Korean Wave), traditional culture experience, information technology need to be developed and managed. Seventh, after the relocation of Korea Tourism Organization’s head quarters, it is suggested that the K-MICE information center be operated in Seoul, a hub for integrated marketing with convention alliance.&#xD; &#xD; This study, despite its significant research value, revealed some limitations. The quantitative Delphi technique was used in order to derive the measurement factors for the destination preference indicator. The study also relies only on the results of statistical analysis to determine the relative importance of attributes. Thus, the study has not been able to determine types of measurement factors based on field experience of industry's working level personnel and weights on relative importance of the factors. The converged measurement factors also show limitations in providing adequate information for the study. &#xD; In addition, the comparative research on the positioning of the destinations, which was performed through the developed indicator, did not overcome the limitations in securing generalizability and transferability of the study’s result due to limited objects for comparison and sample size.&#xD; It is suggested that future studies should conduct a qualitative research with a theoretical basis to overcome the aforementioned limitations. An empirical analysis should also be applied after securing diverse groups and an adequate sample size.본 연구의 목적은 두 가지이다. 첫째는 델파이기법(Delphi technique)을 활용하여 컨벤션 개최지 선호도 지표를 개발하는 것이며, 둘째는 개발된 선호도 지표를 활용하여 아시아 주요 국가들의 컨벤션 개최지로서의 포지셔닝을 실증 분석하는 것이다. 이를 통해 궁극적으로 한국의 컨벤션 개최지 경쟁력 강화를 위한 정책 및 개최지 마케팅 전략 수립을 위한 실효적 근거를 제공하는 것이다.&#xD; 본 연구의 세부 연구 목표는 네 가지로 다음과 같다. &#xD; 첫째, 컨벤션 개최지 선택속성 및 경쟁력, 선호도, 포지셔닝에 대한 문헌연구를 통해 컨벤션 개최지 선호도 측정 지표 개발 및 포지셔닝 비교 연구를 위한 이론적 기반을 구축한다. 둘째, 델파이 조사를 통해 컨벤션 개최지 선호도 측정 지표를 개발하고 타당성을 검증한다. 셋째, 개발된 컨벤션 개최지 선호도 측정 지표를 이용하여 아시아 주요 국가들의 컨벤션 개최지로서의 포지셔닝을 비교 분석한다.&#xD; Prediction_retrieved_article_name_10: Title: 타원곡선 암호 알고리즘을 적용한 U-SIM기반 홈 네트워크 Zigbee 통신에 관한 연구, Abstract: 최근 정보통신기술의 발달로 가정 내의 모든 기기 및 센서를 하나의 네트워크로 통합 관리하는 홈 네트워크 환경이 점점 구체화 되어가고 있다. 미래 유비쿼터스 환경의 궁극적인 목표 중 하나인 홈 네트워크의 개념은 컴퓨터와 기타 정보 가전기기들을 전화선, 전력선 등과 같은 유선 매체와 Zigbee, Bluetooth, Home RF, Wireless Lan, WiBro등과 같은 무선 매체들을 이용하여 연결함으로써 가전기기 사이의 데이터 공유뿐만 아니라, 인터넷 등을 통한 원격제어와 가정 내의 컴퓨터나 정보 가전기기를 네트워크로 연결된 기기를 통제할 수 있도록 하는 것을 말한다[1]. 홈 네트워크의 대표적인 서비스는 사용자가 집 안팎에서 시간과 공간의 제약 없이 가정 내의 가전기기들을 제어하고 모니터링 하며 사용자가 원하는 서비스를 제공하는 것이다. 이러한 홈 네트워크에서 오토메이션 기술을 구현하는 것은 스마트 홈의 기반이 되고 정보통신기기들 사이에 정보를 공유하면서 다양한 멀티미디어 서비스를 제공해 줄 수 있다. 또한 사용자의 요구에 부합하는 다양한 서비스가 지원될 수 있다. 대부분의 차세대 정보가전 기기는 다양한 통신 방식을 지원하게 될 것이다. 이는 정보통신기기의 목적과 기능에 맞는 복수의 통신 방식을 사용한다는 것을 의미하며 복수의 통신 방식을 하나의 네트워크 관리자가 관리할 수 있는 네트워크가 홈 네트워크가 된다. 이러한 홈 네트워크에서 사용자 주변의 물리적 현상을 감지하고 적합한 서비스를 제공하기 위해서는 센서 네트워크를 필요로 한다. 센서 네트워크란 센서 장치에 네트워크 개념을 추가해 사물의 존재 여부 및 위치 등에 대한 정보를 네트워크와 연동, 실시간으로 관리 및 제어하는 네트워크이다[2]. 센서 네트워크는 지리적 또는 물리적으로 사람의 손길이 미치기 힘든 곳에 배포되어 해당 지역을 감시&amp;#12539;관찰하는 용도로 사용되기 때문에 주로 무선매체를 많이 사용하고 있다. &#xD; 무선 센서 네트워크에서 많은 무선 매체가 사용되고 있지만 홈 네트워크의 특성인 확장성과 저 전력성을 지닌 무선 매체는 Zigbee이다. For more than a decade, the distribution utility industry has recognized and increasingly accepted the concept of an advanced distribution management system (ADMS). The distribution network analysis and optimization functions are referred to as advanced applications. However, surprisingly few distribution utilities have successfully implemented an ADMS with advanced applications. Even fewer have system operators making full use of such applications. Numerous small-scale pilot projects have been executed and completed where the value of such advanced applications as fault location isolation and service restoration (FLISR) and integrated volt/volt-ampere reactive optimization (IVVO) have been positively confirmed. Successful systemwide operational deployments of advanced applications, however, are much less common. There are multiple reasons for this, including insufficient numerical robustness of advanced applications to provide solutions under a wide variety of system conditions. Other reasons include model-magnitude, complexity, and data-quality issues.

Prediction_retrieved_article_name_34: Title: 문화기반 농촌지역개발 전략 연구, Abstract: 농촌은 생태환경, 농업, 농촌문화, 공동체 문화 가치를 가진 저밀도 혁신 성장의 무대로 평가되고 있다. 도시가 급속한 양적 팽창을 겪으면서 기반시설 부족, 노후시설 정비 지체, 지역산업 쇠퇴 및 부재, 지역문화 자산 방치, 지역공동체 해체로 고밀도 성장포화 상황에 직면하면서 상대적으로 농촌이 생태 환경을 중심으로 성장 잠재력을 가진 저밀도 경제 성장 공간으로 주목받고 있다.&#xD; 우리나라 농촌정책은 농촌이라는 공간의 가치와 농촌지역민의 삶의 질 증대를 목적으로 농촌융복합산업과 농촌지역개발사업을 중심으로 연간 약 10조원 이상의 예산을 투입하고 있다. 그러나 농촌융복합산업과 농촌지역개발 사업이 주민 참여 및 역량 강화에 기여하는 바가 미진하고 지역자원 발굴 및 개발을 위한 전문성 부족, 서비스혁신 및 품질관리 체계 부재, 내·외부 협력적 네트워크 창출과 상호작용 전략 부재 등의 비판을 받고 있다. 또한, 결과적으로 농촌의 정주 만족도와 인구는 지속적으로 감소하고 있으며, 농촌의 GDP도 불안정하거나 하락하는 추이를 보이고 있다.&#xD; 농촌산업 및 농촌지역개발 사업의 성과가 미진하다는 비판이 존재하는 상황에서 문화적 지역개발은 농촌지역민의 역량을 강화하고 공동체를 강화하며 경제적 활성화를 도모할 수 있는 대안적 전략이 될 수 있다. 문화는 새로운 제품과 서비스의 개발과 혁신에 깊이 연결되어있으며, 소비자의 선택과 의사결정에 적극적으로 개입되기 때문에 지역발전 및 경제성장에 직·간접적인 영향을 미친다는 인식이 널리 인정되면서 지역개발 전략으로 활용되고 있다. &#xD; 문화의 가치를 활용하기 위해 각국의 정부 및 지자체, 기업은 문화예술 관련 정책 및 사업을 적극적으로 추진했으며, 다수 연구자에 의해 다양한 문화적 지역개발 전략 및 방법이 제안되어왔다. 그러나 문화적 지역개발 연구는 개발도상국 또는 구도심의 재생을 위한 방안으로는 적극적으로 활용되었으나, 농촌에 적용한 사례는 미진한 상황이다. 또한, 농촌지역개발 선행연구는 물리적 환경, 사회적 자본, 주민의 지역개발사업 참여의도, 리더십, 호혜성, 지속 가능성 확보 전략이 지역개발에 중요하다고 보고하고 있으나, 문화적 지역개발 전략을 중심으로 농촌지역개발 방안을 검토한 연구는 부족한 실정이다. &#xD; 이에 다음과 같은 연구문제를 설정했다.&#xD; &#xD; 연구문제 1 : 문화기반 농촌지역개발을 위한 중요한 주요요인은 무엇이며, 상대적 중요도는 어떠한가?&#xD; 연구문제 2 : 문화기반 농촌지역개발 비즈니스 생태계 모델은 무엇인가?&#xD; 연구문제 3 : 농촌의 서비스품질, 신뢰, 방문의도의 관계에 대한 소비자 인식은 어떠한가?&#xD; &#xD; 위와 같은 연구문제를 검토하기 위해 본 연구는 연구 1 문화기반 농촌지역개발 주요요인 및 상대적 중요도 분석 연구, 연구 2 문화기반 농촌지역개발 비즈니스 생태계 모델 연구, 연구 3 농촌의 서비스품질과 신뢰가 농촌방문의도에 미치는 영향 연구를 차례로 수행했다.&#xD; 먼저, 연구 1에서는 델파이 분석과 AHP를 결합한 DHP 분석을 활용하여 문화기반 농촌지역개발 주요요인 도출 및 상대적 중요도 분석을 실시했다. 이를 위해 문화기반 농촌지역개발 관련 전문가 18명을 대상으로 1~2차 델파이, 3차 AHP 조사·분석을 실시했다.&#xD; 하였다. 3장에서는 기존 문헌 연구를 통하여 시스템 기술 경쟁 하에서의외부성(Network Externality) 효과와 표준화 전략에 대하여 살펴 보았다. 특히 이동통신시장을 중심으로 망 외부성과 기업의 기술전략(표준)과관련하여 기존의 이론으로 설명하지 못하는 부분을 문제로 제기하였다. 1980년대 중반 이후, 여러 산업에 걸쳐 제품의 모듈화, 산업의융합, 기술적 복잡성 증가와 같은 현상이 나타나면서 제품 표준의중요성이 더욱 중요하게 인식되기 시작하였다. 이러한 인식은 기업의기술전략에도 많은 변화를 가져왔는데, 이러한 변화는 특히 망 외부성을갖는 산업에서 활동을 하고 있는 기업에게 큰 영향을 주었다 (Shapiro andVarian,1999). 시장 경쟁을 통한 사실상 표준의 선점은 기업에게 많은 단, 장기적 경쟁우위를 가져 다 줄 수 있으므로, 기업들은 표준을 선정하기위해 독자적인 기술 개발, 기술의 공개, 몇몇 기업과의 제휴와 같은 전략을사용하기 시작하였다. 기술 공개 전략은 초기의 기술확산을 빠르게 할 수 있는 장점이있지만, 같은 기술을 사용하는 기업이 많아짐으로써 경쟁이 치열해질 수있다는 단점이 존재한다. 이에 비해 독자적 기술 전략은 자신이 기술을직접 컨트롤하고 소비자를 고착화시킬 수 있는 장점이 존재하는 반면,표준으로 선택되지 않았을 경우 시장에서 퇴출될 수 있다는 위험이존재한다. 제휴는 이 두 가지 방식의 흔합형태로서, 제휴를 맺은기업들끼리는 기술을 공유하지만, 그 이외의 기업에게는 기술을 공개하지않는 형태이다. 최근 시스템적인 성격을 지니는 제품이 등장하면서 이러한제휴를 통한 기업군의 경쟁이 점차 증가하는 양상을 보이고 있다. 이러한제휴 형태는 전통적으로 망 외부성을 나타낸다고 인식되어왔던 이동통신산업에서도 나타나서, 현재 전세계적으로는 크게 GSM 방식을 사용하는기업군과 CDMA 방식을 사용하는 기업군의 경쟁 형태를 보이고 있다. 그러나, 이동통신 산업은, 망 외부성을 갖는 다른 산업과는 차별화된 독특한 특징을 점차 나타내고 있다. 기존의 기업군은 각자 자신의시장을 넓히기 위해 경쟁하고 있으나, 중국과 같은 일부 개발도상국들은자국 시장의 보호와 기술의 확보, 독자적 개발을 위하여, 기존 방식과는호환되지 않는 다른 기술을 채택하고 있다. 즉, 망외부성을 보이는산업에서 쉽게 나타난다고 인식되었던 winner-take-all이 나타나지 않고,새로운 기술이 지속적으로 등장하고 있으며, Title: Smart Port Allocation for Adaptive NoC Routers, Abstract:

Network on Chip (NoC) is an emerging communication framework for multiple processing cores on a System on Chip (SoC). The router micro-architecture determines the performance of such a communication network to a great extend. Considering the cost effective performance and scalability, minimally buffered deflection routers are emerging as a popular design choice for NoC based multicore systems. In this paper, a new router architecture is proposed which has an enhanced pipeline register and a smart port allocator that significantly reduces the pipeline stage delay in the router. The proposed smart port allocator assigns output port to incoming flits dynamically based on available output ports and flit occupancy level of the enhanced pipeline register. This eliminates unwanted intra-router movement of flits. Although selection problems are often encountered in engineering practice, rigorous decision analysis techniques remain underutilized in undergraduate chemical engineering education. 주기 위하여 각 요인들의 중요도를 산출해야 한다. 셋째, 각 데이터를 일률적으로 분류하기 위한 적절성 등급과 각 요인들에 부합하는 분류기준을 마련할 필요가 있다. 넷째, 위의 결과를 토대로 강원도 지역에서 풍력발전소가 입지하기에 적절한 지역을 찾고 각 점수별 지역의 특징을 알아본다. 마지막으로 본 연구의 결과와 기존 풍력발전소의 위치를 비교・분석한다. 풍력발전소 입지선정 시 고려해야할 요인들을 도출하기 위하여 풍력발전소 입지선정과 관련된 연구들을 조사하였다. 문헌연구를 통해 도출된 요인들의 객관성과 현장에서의 적용가능성 확보를 위하여 전문가와의 인터뷰를 실시하였으며 이를 통하여 최종적으로 입지선정 요인을 확정하였다. 각 요인들은 상대적으로 다른 중요도를 가지므로 AHP(Analytic Hierarchy Process)기법을 이용하여 요인별 가중치를 산출하였다. 중첩분석을 위하여 풍력발전소가 입지하기에 적절한 정도에 따라 3등급(매우적합-5점, 보통-3점, 미흡-1점)으로 구분하고 각 요인별로 이에 맞는 분류기준을 마련하였다. 데이터에 분류기준과 가중치를 부여한 후 중첩분석을 실시하여 풍력발전소가 입지하기에 적절한 지역을 파악하였다. 분석결과 도출된 점수별 지역의 바람자원 특성을 알아보기 위하여 점수별로 연평균 풍력밀도와 월평균 풍력밀도를 Arc GIS Desktop 9.3을 이용하여 분석하였다. 또한 기존풍력발전단지의 위치를 GIS데이터로 구축하고 이를 이용하여 기존풍력발전단지의 특징과 본 연구결과와의 상관성을 분석하였다.  연구결과는 다음과 같이 요약할 수 있다.  첫째, 풍력발전소 입지선정 시 고려해야 할 요인으로 총 11개의 요인이 도출되었다. 분석을 용이하게 하기 위하여 도출된 요인들을 크게 자연적 요인, 환경보호 요인, 인간피해 요인, 경제적 요인으로 분류하였다. 자연적 요인으로는 바람자원, 지형(골짜기 각도, 능선까지의 거리), 산림밀도를 고려하였으며, 환경보호 요인으로는 토지이용, 보존지역, 국립공원, 백두대간을 고려하였다. 인간피해 요인으로는 소음과 그림자를 고려하였으며, 경제적 요인으로는 송전선로, 접근도로를 고려하였다. 둘째, AHP기법을 이용하여 요인별 중요도를 산출한 결과 Level 2에서는 자연적 요인(65%)이 가장 높은 중요도를 가진 것으로 도출되었으며, 다음으로 경제적 요인(19%), 환경보호 요인(11%)이 높게 나타났으며 인간피해 요인(5%)이 가장 낮은 중요도를 가진 것으로 나타났다. 세부분류 항목(Level 3)에서는 각 요인별로 중요도가 산출되었는데, 자연적 요인에서는 바람자원(68%)이 가장 높은 중요도를 보였으며 다음으로 능선까지의 거리(16%), 골짜기 각도(9%), 산림밀도(7%)가 차례대로 높게 나타났다. 환경보호 요인에서는 토지이용(41%)이 가장 중요도가 높았고, 국립공원(27%)과 백두대간(22%)이 비슷한 비율로 높게 나타났으며, 보존지역(10%)이 가장 낮은 중요도를 가진 것으로 나타났다. 인간피해 요인에서는 소음(50%)과 그림자(50%)가 같은 중요성을 가진 것으로 나타났다. 경제적 요인은 송전선로(62%)가 접근도로(38%)에 비해 상대적으로 더 중요한 것으로 나타났다.  셋째, 본 연구에서는 풍력발전소 입지선정 시 고려해야 할 요인을 크게 4가지의 대분류 항목으로 구분하였으며 그 아래 총11개의 세부항목을 두었다. 그리고 각 세부 항목에 부합하는 데이터를 구축하였다. 그러나 각 데이터는 각자 다른 단위의 정보를 가지고 있으며 연속적인 데이터이므로 중첩분석을 용이하게 하기 위해서는 일률적인 적절성 등급으로 구분할 필요가 있다. 이에 풍력발전기가 입지하기에 적절한 정도에 따라 ‘매우 적합’, ‘보통’, ‘미흡’으로 구분하였으며, ‘매우적합’에 5점, ‘보통’에 3점, ‘미흡’에 1점을 부여하였다. 그리고 기존연구와 전문가 의견을 바탕으로 각 데이터에 대한 분류 기준점을 제시하였다. 넷째, 강원도 지역을 중심으로 중첩분석을 실시한 결과 1점부터 5점까지의 지역이 도출되었다. 5점 지역은 가장 높은 점수를 받은 지역으로 본 논문의 기준으로 보았을 때 풍력발전소가 입지하기에 가장 적절한 지역이라고 할 수 있다. 5점을 받은 지역은 대부분 고도 600m 이상에 있는 능선을 따라 존재하는 경향이 있었다. 4점과 5점 지역이 대부분 태백산맥 산지에 몰려있어 상대적으로 고도가 높은 태백산맥 지역이 풍력발전을 하기에 유리한 지역임을 알 수 있었다. 점수별 지역이 어떤 특징을 가지고 있는지 알기 위하여 점수별로 분석을 실시한 결과 5점 지역이 다른 점수를 받은 지역에 비하여 매우 탁월한 조건을 갖추고 있음을 알 수 있었다. 그러나 5점 지역은 산림밀도가 높고 생태자연도 1등급 지역이 많으며, 백두대간 핵심구역도 일부 속해있어 풍력발전소 건립 시 환경적인 측면에서 건립허가에 어려움이 예상된다.  다섯째, 풍력발전 입지선정 시 가장 중요한 것이 바람자원인 만큼 점수별 지역의 바람자원을 파악하는 것이 중요하다. 이에 바람자원을 평가하는데 가장 대표적으로 사용되는 풍력밀도(W/㎡)를 이용하여 점수별 바람자원을 파악하였다. 연평균 풍력밀도를 분석해본 결과 1점 지역이 127.64W/㎡, 2점지역이 137.31W/㎡ 3점 지역이 243.27W/㎡, 4점 지역이 554.27W/㎡, 5점 지역이 546.46W/㎡로 나타났다. 대형풍력발전기가 400W/㎡이상인 곳에 세워지도록 권장된다는 사실로 비춰봤을 때 4점과 5점 지역에 세우는 것이 적절할 것으로 보인다. 점수별로 월별 평균 풍력밀도를 구하여 비교해본 결과 봄, 가을, 겨울에는 풍력밀도가 높게 나타났으나 여름에는 확연히 낮아져 월별로 그 격차가 큰 것을 확인할 수 있었다.   여섯째, 풍력발전소 적지 분석을 통해 도출된 결과와 기존 풍력발전단지의 위치를 비교해본 결과 강원도에 위치한 6개의 풍력발전 단지는 3점, 4점, 5점 지역에 위치하고 있었다. 태기산 풍력발전단지와 양양풍력발전 단지를 제외한 모든 풍력발전단지가 1000m 이상의 고지대에 위치하고 있었으며, 풍력발전단지 대부분이 능선에 위치한 것으로 나타나 고지대 능선이 풍력발전을 하기에 적절한 장소임을 알 수 있었다. 기존 풍력발전단지의 위치가 5점 지역만이 아닌 3점, 4점 지역에 위치하는 것은 정부정책이나 회사의 정책에 따라 중요시하는 가치가 다르기 때문으로 생각된다. 본 논문에서 입지분석을 위한 도구로 GIS를 이용함에 따라 풍력발전소 입지선정 시 고려해야할 요인들 중 공간데이터로 구축되기 어려운 요인들은 고려대상에서 제외되었다는 점에서 한계가 있다. 또한 설문의 대상이 주로 풍력발전소 운영자이다 보니 가중치가 경제적인 측면에 치우치는 경향이 있었다. 풍력발전단지가 우리 모두의 자산인 국토를 이용하는 만큼 다양한 전문가들의 의견이 함께 고려될 필요가 있을 것으로 보인다. 그러나 본 논문은 풍력발전소의 입지를 선정하는데 고려해야 할 다양한 요인들을 각각 따로 고려해야 하는 번거로움 없이 AHP와 GIS를 이용하여 동시에 고려할 수 있도록 했다는데 그 의의가 있다. GIS는 위치를 기반으로 하므로 도출된 지역의 분포를 바로 확인할 수 있으며 장소의 특징을 파악하기가 용이하다. 또한 본 연구에서는 연구과정을 모델로 구축하여 시대와 상황에 따라 변하는 가중치와 기준을 바로 적용하여 분석할 수 있도록 하였다. 본 연구는 풍력발전소의 후보지를 개략적으로 도출하기 위한 것으로 풍력발전소의 입지를 최종결정하기 위해서는 후보지에 대한 1년 이상의 사후조사가 필요하다. 이처럼 하나의 풍력발전소가 세워지기 위해서는 오랜 기간의 사전조사와 이에 대한 평가가 필요하다. 이것은 풍력발전기의 경우 한 번 세워지면 장소이동이 어렵기 때문이다. 이처럼 풍력발전소의 경우 입지선정이 매우 중요함에도 불구하고 우리나라에서는 풍력발전소 입지선정에 대한 연구가 많이 이뤄지고 있지 않다. 풍력발전기 증대라는 계획을 세우기에 앞서 우리나라 현실에 적합한 세부적인 기준들을 마련할 필요가 있다. 국가적으로 풍력발전기를 세우기 위한 세부적인 기준들이 마련될 때 우리나라 풍력사업은 한 걸음 성장할 수 있을 것이다., Source: http://click.ndsl.kr/servlet/OpenAPIDetailView?keyValue=DIKO0012276227&target=NART&cn=DIKO0012276227

Title: On Consistency in AHP and Fuzzy AHP, Abstract:

Abstract

The analytic hierarchy process (AHP) is used widely for analyzing decisions made in various real-world applications. Its basic idea is to construct a hierarchy of concepts encountered in a given decision problem and to choose the best alternative according to pairwise comparison matrices given by the decision maker. Under the assumption of fully rational economics, a reasonable decision should be consistent. It becomes an important issue on how to analyze and ensure the consistency of comparison matrices together with the judgments of the decision maker. The main objectives of the present paper are threefold. First, we review the basic idea and methods used to define the consistency and the transitivity of multiplicative reciprocal matrices, additive reciprocal matrices and comparison matrices with fuzzy interval and triangular fuzzy numbers. The existing controversy behind the applications of fuzzy set theory to the AHP in the literature is presented. Second, the consistency of the collective comparison matrices in group decision making based on AHP and fuzzy AHP is further analyzed. We point out that the weak consistency of preference relations with fuzzy numbers in fuzzy AHP and group decision making should be investigated comprehensively. Third, under the consideration of the vagueness in the process of evaluating the judgements, a new concept of fuzzy consistency of comparison matrices in the AHP is given.

Prediction_retrieved_article_name_14: Title: 고혈압 쥐의 주요 조직에서의 Cytochrome P450 발현 변화, Abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP 또는 P450) 효소는 자연계의 거의 모든 생물종 (식물, 박테리아, 동물 등)에서 발견되며 대략 45,000~60,000 Da 정도의 분자량을 갖는 heme-containing protein이다. 포유동물에서는 주로 간세포의 endoplasmic reticulum 막에 존재하는 것으로 알려져 있으며 체외 물질 (xenobiotics)의 산화를 촉매하는 주요 효소 체계이다. 또한 지방산의 대사 및 steroids, eicosanoids, bile acids, fat-soluble vitamins 등 체내물질(endobiotics)의 대사에도 관여한다. 이와 같이 광범위한 물질 대사에 관여하는 P450의 발현 양과 활성은 동물의 경우 종에 따라, 연령과 성별 등에 따라 다르며 동일한 개체에서도 영양 상태와 외부 환경 및 병적 상태 등에 따라 달라지며 각종 약물과 호르몬에 의해서도 변동이 있다. 그러므로 xenobiotics와 endobiotics의 대사에 중요한 CYP과 질병과의 관계는 중요한 연구 과제가 되었다. 그 예로 대사성 질환(metabolic syndrome)중 하나로서 신장(kidney)과 뇌의(cerebral) 질환, 심장 질환 (coronary heart disease)의 위험인자가 되는 고혈압(hypertension)과 CYP의 연관성에 대한 연구가 이루어져있다. 그러나 arachidonic acid 대사와 관련된 CYP의 연구에 초점을 맞추고 있을 뿐 간에서 발현되는 CYPs에 대한 연구는 보고되어 있지 않다. 그러므로 본 연구를 통해서 한국인에게서 특히 발병률이 높은 고혈압의 질환 모델 SHR (spontaneously hypertensive rat)에서 간에서 발현되는 주요 CYP 효소군의 단백체적 접근을 통해 상호 연계성을 밝히고자 하였다. Aromatase is the cytochrome P450 enzyme converting androgens into estrogen in the last phase of steroidogenesis. As estrogens are crucial in reproductive biology, aromatase is found in vertebrates and the invertebrates of the genus Branchiostoma, where it carries out the aromatization reaction of the A-ring of androgens that produces estrogens. Adversarial attacks pose a threat to deep learning models. However, research on adversarial detection methods, especially in the multi-modal domain, is very limited. Prediction_retrieved_article_name_3: Title: 서로 다른 아데노신 수용체 아형 활성화에 의한 심방이뇨 호르몬의 특이적 분비 조절, Abstract: 아데노신은 체내 여러 조직과 세포에 광범위하게 존재하고 있으며 국부빈혈, 저산소증과 같은 체내환경에서 대량으로 생성된다. 아데노신은 자체의 특이한 수용체들을 통하여 심혈관계에서 관상혈관을 이완시키고 심근수축력과 심박동수를 감소시키는 등 중요한 생리적기능을 하며 심혈관의 조직과 세포가 손상되지 않도록 보호해 준다. 아데노신 뿐만 아니라 아데노신과 유사한 구조를 갖고 있는 여러가지 약물들도 아데노신의 특이한 수용체들을 통하여 심혈관계에서 중요한 작용을 나타낸다. 한편 심방은 심방이뇨호르몬 (atrial natriuretic peptide, ANP) 을 합성하고 분비하는 주된 장소이며 ANP는 레닌-안지오텐신-알도스테론계 (renin-angio- tensin-aldosterone system, RAAS) 와 함께 체액조절에 깊이 관여한다. 여러가지 요인들이 ANP분비조절에 영향을 미치는데 그 중에서도 심방 역동성의 변동이 주된 원인이다. 따라서 아데노신 수용체 활성화에 의한 심혈관계의 변동은 ANP분비조절과 밀접한 관계가 있을 것이다. 현재 아데노신 특이한 수용체들을 경유한 여러가지 중요한 생리적작용과 신호전달체계들이 끊임없는 연구들을 통하여 꾸준히 밝혀지고 있지만 아데노신 수용체 활성화에 의한 ANP분비조절과 그 기전에 대해서는 아직도 잘 알려지지 않고 있다. 이 연구의 목적은 박동하는 심방관류모형에서 아데노신과 유사한 구조를 갖고 있는 diadenosine polyphosphates (APnAs) 와 아데노신A₃ 수용체 선택적 작동제인 2-chloro-N^(6)- (3-iodobenzyl) adenosine-5’-N-methyluronamide (2-Cl-IB-MECA) 를 사용하여 아데노신 수용체 활성화에 의한 심방 수축력의 변동과 ANP분비 조절, 및 그 기전을 구명하고자 하였다. 정상백서의 좌측 심방을 분리하여 박동하는 심방관류모형을 만들었으며 지속적으로 HEPES완충액을 관류하였고 1.3 HZ의 빈도로 전기자극 하였다. A₃수용체 선택적 길항제인MRS 1220으로 전처리 하였을 때에 2-CI-IB-MECA에 의한 ANP분비 증가 효과는 차단되었으나 A₁ 또는 A₂A수용체 선택적 길항제인 DPCPX와 ZM 241385로 전처리 하였을 때에는 영향 받지 않았다. 2-CI-IB-MECA에 의한 심방 수축력, 세포외액 이동량과ANP분비 증가 효과는 ryanodine receptor, calcium/calmodulin-dependent kinase II (CaMKII) 또는 AC 억제제들로 전처리 하였을 때에는 약화되었지만 L-type Ca^(2+) channel, sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) Ca^(2+)-reuptake, PLC 또는 inositol 1,4,5-triphosphate (IP3₃) receptor 억제제들로 전처리 하였을 때에는 영향을 받지 않았다. 2-CI-IB-MECA에 의한 cAMP감소 효과는 CaMKII와 AC 억제제들로 전처리 하였을 때에만 차단되었다. 2K1C 신성 고혈압 백서에서 2-CI-IB-MECA에 의한 ANP증가 효과는 강화되었으며 ANP증가 효과와 수축기 혈압 사이에는 양성의 상관관계가 있었다. 이상의 결과로부터AP₄A는 A₁수용체를 경유한 PLC-PKC, sarcolemmal KATP channel, 그리고 PKA등 신호전달체계를 통하여 심방 수축력과 ANP분비 조절에 깊이 관여하고 있음을 알 수 있었다. 그리고 신성 고혈압 백서에서AP₄A에 의한 ANP분비 증가 효과 약화는A₁ receptor 수용체의 하향조절과 관련이 있을 것이라 사료된다. 또한2-CI-IB-MECA에 의한 심방 수축력 증가 효과와 ANP분비 증가 효과는 A₃ 수용체를 경유한 ryanodine receptor, CaMKII활성화와 세포 내 Ca^(2+) 조절을 통하여 나타남을 알 수 있었다. 뿐만 아니라 신성 고혈압 백서에서2-CI-IB-MECA에 의한 ANP분비 증가의 강화는A₃ receptor 수용체의 상향조절과 관련이 있을 것이라 사료된다., Source: http://click.ndsl.kr/servlet/OpenAPIDetailView?keyValue=DIKO0011275089&target=NART&cn=DIKO0011275089
Prediction_retrieved_article_name_4: Title: A₃adenosine 수용체에 선택적인 아데노신 유도체의 항염증 효과와 항암 활성 및 그 작용기전에 관한 연구, Abstract: 아데노신 (adenosine) 은 세포 내에서 ATP 분해에 의해 생성되는 것으로 세포내의 아데노신이 축적이 되면 세포 외로 방출되는데 염증 관련 질환, 허혈성 심 질환 및 조직 손상과 같은 병태 생리학적 과정이 있을 경우 세포 내에서 ATP의 대사는 더 활발해 지고 그 결과 아데노신의 방출이 증가한다고 알려져 있다. 아데노신은 아데노신 수용체를 경유하여 신호 전달을 하게 되는데 아데노신 수용체에는 4종류, A1, A2A, A2B and A₃ 가 존재하고 있다. 특히, A₃ adenosine receptor (A₃AR)는 효능제는 항암 및 항염증 활성이 있으며 길항제 역시 항염증 활성을 지닌다고 알려져 있다. 아데노신 유도체로 A₃AR에 선택적인 효능제인 2-chloro-N6-(3-iodobenzyl)-4’-thioadenosine-5’-N-methyluronamide (thio-Cl-IB-MECA) 와 선택적인 길항제인 LJ-1888를 이용하여 마우스 유래 대식 세포인 RAW 264.7 세포에서의 항염증 활성을 알아보고 염증성 동물 모델에서 효과를 알아보았다. 먼저 lipopolysaccharide (LPS)로 염증 반응을 유도한 RAW 264.7 세포에 아데노신 유도체를 처리하고 NO 생성 저해 활성을 평가한 결과 thio-Cl-IB-MECA의 IC50 값은 16.23 μM, LJ-1888의 IC50 값은 10.16 μM 이었다. 따라서 아데노신 유도체의 항염증 활성에 관한 작용 기전을 추가적으로 연구한 결과 염증성 물질인 inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), interleukine-1β (IL-1β), tumor necrosis factor (TNF-α) 와 cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) 의 mRNA 및 단백질 발현이 모두 저해되었다. 또한 염증성 물질의 유전자 발현에 영향을 미치는 LPS에 의해 매개되는 신호 전달 경로를 알아본 결과, 전사 인자인 NF-κB의 subunit인 p65의 결합을 방해하여 핵 내에서 NF-κB의 DNA 결합도 저해하였고, NF-κB의 핵 내 이동을 저해하는 IκB분해도 저해하였다. Title: Role of A3 adenosine receptor in diabetic neuropathy, Abstract:

Neuropathy is the most common diabetic complication. Although the A1 and A2A adenosine receptors are important pharmacological targets in alleviating diabetic neuropathy, the role of the A3 adenosine receptor remains unknown. Because the A3 adenosine receptor regulates pain induced by chronic constriction injury or chemotherapy, its stimulation might also attenuate diabetic neuropathy. This study examines the effects of systemic treatment with the A3 adenosine receptor agonist 1‐deoxy‐1‐[6‐[[(3‐iodophenyl)methyl]amino]‐9H‐purin‐9‐yl]‐N‐methyl‐β‐d‐ribofuranuronamide (IB‐MECA) on diabetic neuropathy and explores the putative mechanisms underlying its pharmacological effects. We show that IB‐MECA alleviated mechanical hyperalgesia and thermal hypoalgesia in mice 2 weeks but not 4 weeks after streptozocin (STZ) treatment. Furthermore, IB‐MECA prevented the reduction in sciatic motor nerve conduction velocity and sensory nerve conduction velocity in diabetic mice 2 weeks but not 4 weeks after STZ treatment. Similarly, IB‐MECA inhibited the activation of nuclear factor‐κB and decreased the generation of tumor necrosis factor‐α in the spinal cord of mice 2 weeks but not 4 weeks after STZ treatment. These phenomena were associated with reduction of A3 adenosine receptor expression in the spinal cord after long‐term diabetes. Our results suggest that the A3 adenosine receptor plays a critical role in regulating diabetic neuropathy and that reduction in A3 adenosine receptor expression/function might contribute to the progression of diabetic neuropathy. © 2016 Wiley Periodicals, Inc.

Title: A3-A3 Bypass Surgery for Aneurysm: Technical Nuances, Abstract:

Abstract

BACKGROUND

Cerebral bypass remains important for the treatment of complex cerebral aneurysms including dissecting, giant, and fusiform aneurysms not amenable to endovascular treatment or simple clip ligation. For such aneurysms involving the anterior communicating artery complex or its branches, distal anterior cerebral artery (ACA) A3-A3 side-to-side bypass represents a valuable treatment option. Distal ACA in situ anastomosis is recognized to be technically demanding mainly due to the relative depth and narrowness of the interhemispheric surgical corridor and type of anastomosis.

OBJECTIVE

To demonstrate technical nuances of A3-A3 side-to-side in situ bypass surgery through case illustrations and operative videos.

METHODS

Elements of the procedure relating to positioning, approach, and anastomosis which have evolved in the operative technique of the senior author were collated based on review of clinical case material, imaging and video recordings of ACA aneurysms treated with side-to-side in situ A3-A3 bypass procedure. Technical elements were contrasted with relevant literature.

RESULTS

Nuances relative to patient positioning, selection of craniotomy variants, adjunctive intraoperative tools and microsurgical nuances of the side-to-side bypass procedure are reviewed. Three illustrative operative video cases, along with illustrations, are provided to complement the description of the nuances.

CONCLUSION

In the light of the inherent technical difficulty, as well as the rather limited case volumes, the technical tips provided may contribute to bringing additional refinement and simplicity to the A3-A3 bypass procedure.
